- F-143 **Under walk, a type parameter whose bound mentions itself and that nothing at a call fixes is left open.** Such a bound is an F-bound, as in `mk[\T extends Cmp[\T\]\]()`. The open type is below every type, and every value matches it. A reduction or a comprehension that writes no static argument is first instantiated by its declared type or by its elements' join (F-228). So the open parameter reaches one only where neither fixes it, as in an empty reduction that no declared type directs, which takes `ZZ32`'s identity (row 716). A call such as `mk()` also leaves it open. A tuple, arrow or generic type that holds the open type admits no more than it would at `BottomType`, so `(Int, Int)` is not below `(OPEN, OPEN)` (row 663, contested). In a skeptic's probe, a declaration whose parameter type is the open type was the most specific one, and so was chosen for every argument; no gated test holds this. Gated by `tests/InferUnfixedFBoundedWalk.fss` and `OpenTupleDispatchWalk.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-open-param/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 11; its `SKEPTIC.md` section 3, finding 3 (the probe).
- F-144 **The identity-less reductions are typed at their element type: `AssociativeReduction[\R\]` lifts to `Maybe[\R\]`, and its `simpleJoin` and every `lift` take `R`.** A reduction that extends `AssociativeReduction` declares `simpleJoin` at its element type; walk refuses one at `Any` at load. One with static parameters escapes that check and stops at its first join (row 665). A static argument that names the lifted type is `Maybe[\R\]`, since walk refuses `AnyMaybe` there. With the element type unwritten, `BIG MINMAX` and the four tuple forms run under walk. A plain-bounded monoid operator with no static argument is instantiated as F-228 says: in one measurement each, `BIG SQCUP`, `BIG SQCAP` and `List`'s nested `BIG CONCAT` ran; `PrefixSet`'s `BIG UNION` and `PureList`'s `BIG CONCAT` were not measured, and no gated test holds any of them. Gated by `tests/Unwritten*Walk.fss` and `ReductionSimpleJoinAtAnyWalk` (the refusal at `Any`). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-reduction-types/REPORT.md` section 1; `compile-ladder/rung-walk-elements/REPORT.md` section 7 (the operators that ran).
- F-145 **Walk refuses at load an object that leaves an inherited abstract method uncovered.** Bodies at narrower parameter types define an abstract method only where together they cover its parameter types, with `comprises` clauses read, as P-147 decides: each position is split through the clauses, and every combination of parts must lie inside one body. A search that does not settle refuses the object: a cycle, a symbolic or unreadable type, 10,000 steps or 4,096 combinations. A generic object is not checked (row 665), and an object whose one covering definition has a static parameter of its own is refused (row 728). The compiled checker covers the same way, within the same bounds, except where a method has static parameters of its own (row 725). Walk's other checks at load of an object are the `override` check (F-147) and the Meet Rule for Functional Methods (F-142). Gated by `tests/AbstractMethod*Walk` (`AbstractMethodCoverUnsettledWalk` among them) and `compiler_tests/AbstractMethodCoveredPairs`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-coverage/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 6 (the cover); `compile-ladder/rung-duplicates-coverage/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 8 (the refusal of a search that does not settle, which replaced the first report's acceptance).
- F-146 **The compiled checker accepts arithmetic in a size, and compares two sizes by their written form once it has computed each operation on numerals.** It builds P-55. A size name or an operation beside a numeral counts as possibly equal to it. Two different size parameters count as different sizes: the checker calls a `typecase` clause unreachable that walk reaches at equal arguments (row 683, contested). Neither path infers a static parameter that a parameter type writes inside an operation (row 767). The compiled class loader can make a size beyond its kind, where walk refuses it (row 675). Gated by `compiler_tests/NatArith*`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-size-expressions/REPORT.md` section 1, "Item 15, 15a with its part (b)", and section 12.
- F-?1 **The compiled checker opens a value of a trait whose `comprises` clause lists a type at a `where`-clause size: it gives each listed type's `nat` and `int` `where`-clause sizes a fresh name for the call.** In `trait NatParam comprises { N[\n\] } where [\ nat n \]`, a `NatParam` passed where `N[\$n\]` is expected binds `$n` to the fresh size, and the call's result type carries it. An opened size is not known to differ from any size. Walk reads such a `where`-clause size as any size. This is a default, way 4a of PLAN item 13's fork 3 (a size known only at run time), landed by an agent; it waits for the curator's review (P-85; review-queue item 30). An opened size does not compile (row 307). The checker refuses `f(x: NatParamT)` beside `f[\nat n\](x: Nt[\n\])` as two declarations of one parameter type, where walk runs the pair (row 682, contested). F-251 holds the same opening for a type variable. Gated by `compiler_tests/NatOpenChecker`, and under walk by `tests/NatOpenWalk` and `NatOpenUnlistedExtender`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-size-expressions/REPORT.md` section 1, "Fork 3, way 4a, under Q13.3", and section 12.
- F-147 **Walk refuses an `override` that overrides nothing; an inherited declaration is overridden only where each of its parameter types is a subtype of the `override`'s and not all are equal.** This is the traits chapter's "strict subtype" (`Specification/basic/traits.tex:585-589`). Walk checks the `override` of a trait, object or object expression with static parameters once, at its declaration. An object inherits nothing that a trait's `override` overrides, so an abstract `override` leaves it without a body (rows 614, 649). Walk does not read all the bounds of the static parameters in an object expression, which takes them from the function around it, or in a generic trait or object that extends a type under a `where` clause. There it accepts an `override` over an inherited declaration whose parameter types mention a static parameter and differ from the `override`'s (row 693). The `fortress-repo` skill gives the rule's other cases (`references/interpreter.md`, "What walk checks"). Gated by `tests/Override*Walk.fss` and `AbstractOverrideUndefinedWalk`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-override/REPORT.md` section 1.
- F-228 **Under walk, a reduction or a comprehension that writes no static argument instantiates its big operator by a declared type, else by the join of its elements' run-time types, else at its bound, where an F-bounded parameter stays open.** It builds P-48. The declared type is a local variable's, or a top-level or local function's declared return type, also where the clause form ends a block. A method's return type, a top-level variable, a field, an assignment, a function expression, a branch, a call's argument and another clause form's body do not direct it. Otherwise the clauses run once into the library's collector, and the operator is instantiated at the elements' join; the reduction then runs over the collected elements, so each body runs once. With no element and no declared type, a plain-bounded static parameter takes its bound, and an F-bounded one stays open (F-143). A big operator whose declared result is a trait of its own is read through the `BigReduction`, `Comprehension` or `BigOperator` that the trait extends. So `__bigOperator`'s `body(i: I)` is typed. Left open: an empty clause form that no declared type directs (row 716), a comprehension that no declared type reaches (rows 20 and 717), and an argument of a call (rows 510 and 705). Gated by `tests/UnwrittenListMapComprehensionWalk`, `UnwrittenComprehension*Walk`, `ComprehensionTypedBindingWalk`, `UnwrittenSetBigOperatorsWalk`, `UnwrittenEmptyFloatSumWalk`, `IntMapComprehensionTypedWalk` and `UserBigOperatorResultTraitWalk`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-elements/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 5 (5.3 lists the contexts); `compile-ladder/rung-walk-overload-if/REPORT.md` section 1, "Row 718".
- F-238 **Under walk's load check, an exclusion that two generic declarations show only at one shared symbolic instantiation is withdrawn where their instances do not exclude.** Walk reads two generic functions of one name and one list of static parameters at one shared symbolic instantiation, and two instances of one generic object as two object types, which exclude. So `o[\T\](x: P[\T\])` beside `o[\T\](x: Q[\T\])`, with `trait P[\T\] excludes { Q[\T\] }`, excludes at one `T`, though a type that extends `P[\ZZ32\]` and `Q[\String\]` has both. Where both declarations have static parameters of their own, walk reads such an exclusion again over the instances of each. Instances of one generic type exclude only where their static arguments cannot be equal. Any other exclusion read at the shared instantiation stands only where every generic type that both extend forces one instance, as `Array` and `ImmutableArray` exclude at every pair of instances through `ReadableArray`. A pair whose exclusion is withdrawn goes on to the reading on declared domains (F-252), and a refusal there names the rule that the pair breaks (F-257). Gated by `tests/GenericBoundsNoMeetWalk`, `NoDuplicatesRuleWalk`, `NoDuplicatesRuleSizeWalk`, `GenericOverloadInstancesApartWalk` (refused), `GenericBoundsMeetWalk`, `GenericFBoundsMeetWalk`, `GenericPairExcludingWalk`, `GenericSizePairNestedWalk`, `ShuffleTest` and `GenericPairExcludesTogetherWalk` (load). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-overload-if/REPORT.md` section 1, "Row 373", and section 9.
- F-239 **Under walk, an `if` clause without a binding takes a `Boolean` by its value, an object named `Just` of a trait named `Maybe` as true and one named `Nothing` as false, and refuses every other value, "If clause did not return boolean".** Walk tests the names only, so a `Just` is true whatever it holds. The refused values are a number, a string, `()`, a tuple, a function, and an object that is neither a `Just` nor a `Nothing`. A refusal while a top-level variable is initialised counts as a refusal at load. The chapter's rule is `Boolean` only (row 746). Gated by `tests/IfClauseObjectWalk`, `IfClauseNumberWalk`, `IfClauseStringWalk`, `maybeTest` and `naturalsTest`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-overload-if/REPORT.md` section 1, "Row 673".
- F-248 **Under walk, the library's generic `distribute[\K\]` keeps every fused answer of a nested reduction, and a nested reduction without a fused pair runs.** A nested reduction is fused where the outer reduction distributes over the inner one, so the library takes a faster path. The library declares the team's generic, `distribute[\K\](r: ActualReduction[\R,K\]): PossibleReductionPair[\K\]`, with no method over `Any` beside it. `GeneratorDeclarations` and microGPT's quick pair keep their answers, and `MAX` and `MIN` over `SUM`, and `SUM` over `PROD`, still take the fused path. A pair that does not fuse, such as a `SUM` of `SUM`s over a generator of generators, runs only because walk infers a generic method's static arguments (F-253); without that inference it stops (row 21). `NestedReductionFusion` asserts 11 for the sum of the prefix sums of 1, 3, 2, and 3 for the maximum of their prefix maxima. The team's commented line in `Generator2.distributes`, the explicit `r.distribute[\L1\](q)`, would stop every fused pair under walk (row 744); the library does not run it. Gated by `tests/GeneratorDeclarations` and `NestedReductionFusion`. Detail: `perf-probes/generic-distribute/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 5.

== explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md, ## Decisions on record, ### The one library and the compiled checker

POSITIONS.md:55
- P-58 **Every native binding is a `builtinPrimitive` call naming a static helper.** A native binding is a library body that is exactly `builtinPrimitive("…")`, the library's own form, and it keeps that form. Its string is to name a static Java method in `nativeHelpers/`, the compiled path's helpers, such as `"com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleIntArith.intLT"`, in place of a glue class of walk, which the compiled path cannot use (F-32). Walk is to load the named helper through a loader beside its glue classes. At the parse, before the checker, the compiled path is to rewrite each such body into a synthetic `import java` of the helper and a call, and to refuse a string that names no helper. The bindings move onto helpers rung by rung, and the compiled checker sees each rung's bindings as that rung lands, not all at once at the switch-over. The other form, `import java` declarations written in the library itself, is not taken. Still to build: all of it. Every binding still names a glue class, and neither the loader nor the rewrite exists. The first natives rung builds them, test first, and the later rungs move the bindings (PLAN, phase 4, "The natives").

POSITIONS.md:39
- P-42 **A type parameter declared without a bound has the implicit bound `Any`, not `Object`.** `Any` holds tuples, functions and `()`, which `Object` does not. The library instantiates its generic containers at tuple types: its arrays indexed by pairs, such as `(ZZ32,ZZ32)`, are among them. The specification states the bound `Any`, with a callout that records that the Working Draft of February 2011 said `Object`. Built in the library and walk. The compiled path departs from it until the switch-over, which ends the departure: while it uses the compiler's prelude, it bounds such a parameter by `Object`, and so refuses a generic instantiated at a tuple (gap-ledger row 412).

36	- **The record's shape is not needed.** The 2026-09-20 note chose one api with a builtin component per path (`import-java-interpreter.md:43-47`). 39	
40	The one library binds every native with `builtinPrimitive("…")`. That construct can serve as the one text too, if its string names a static helper instead of a glue class. 5:These are two small hand-written Java classes. Each holds the elements of one of the only two array-like types the compiled path has: a vector of 32-bit integers and a vector of strings. They are the run-time objects behind the Fortress types `ZZ32Vector` and `StringVector`, and those types exist only in the compiled path's own standard library. Christine Flood wrote both classes in August and September 2011. Guy Steele extended the integer one in October 2011.

The custom class loader (`runtimeSystem/InstantiatingClassloader.java`) makes each instance, for example `Cell⟦FZZ32Vector⟧`, by rewriting the template's bytes the first time that name is asked for. It renames. It does not change field representation (`explorations/coordinator/map/compile-path-walkthrough.md` §6).
27:  - The *gate* is `ant testFast` plus `ant testSystem` with zero failures. A test is *gated* if the gate runs it.

87:### ZZ32Vector

99:  - `__makeZZ32Vector(l1, d1, l2, d2)` is in the builtin api (`.fsi:589`, `.fss:1150`).

- F-173 **The specification's type-inference chapter states the rule that the compiled checker builds: the declaration is chosen first, then its static arguments are inferred.** It states P-46, P-48 and P-49. A type parameter that is the whole declared type of one or more parameters, as `T` is of `x: T`, takes the narrowest of those arguments' types and the types to which they can be coerced; where none is narrowest, it takes its bound. A type parameter that nothing fixes takes its bound, never `BottomType`. The chapter's callouts give two departures of the compiled path: its prelude lacks the conversion between `ZZ32` and `NN32` (row 442), and it bounds a type parameter written without an `extends` clause by `Object`, not `Any` (row 412, P-42). They also give walk's departures, such as the `BottomType` result of a function expression that declares no return type (row 587) (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:292-295` and `:356-425`). Plain tests gate the first rule on both paths: `compiler_tests/InferLone*` and `tests/InferLone*Walk.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-instance-bound/REPORT.md` (the bound rule); `Specification/basic/inference.tex:47-124` (the chapter's rule).
- F-174 **The specification states the type group's 2011 overloading model: declarations of one name may differ in their static parameters, and a declaration with static parameters is read over its instances.** It states P-45 and P-42. The section "Declarations with Static Parameters" states the OOPSLA 2011 paper's three rules: No Duplicates, Return Type and Meet. It gives one more restriction as the compiled path's, not the language's: where one generic declaration is more specific than another with as many static parameters, the two must declare them of the same kinds, position by position (row 398). A functional whose single parameter's type is a type parameter with the bound `Any` written, as `T extends Any`, cannot be overloaded; a type parameter with no `extends` clause does not fall under this rule, and walk applies it (row 534, fixed). Neither path runs every set that the rules allow. Appendix I's entry "Overloading with static parameters" names the sets that each path fails: row 542 (the checker, a more specific declaration over an object type), row 537 (the code generator, two declarations whose bounds differ), row 539 (walk, the Meet Rule's search), and rows 779 and 780 (walk, two generic functional methods one inside the other). Detail: `Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:134-150` and `:531-674`; `compile-ladder/rung-spec-overloading/decision-record.md` sections 3 and 4.
- F-175 **The specification reads a `comprises` clause at the level of values in every passage.** It builds P-60. Appendix I's entry "Traits with comprises clauses read at the level of values" records the change. Appendix I names the compiled checker's departures from it: the checker checks a `comprises` clause at the closed trait's immediate subtypes only (row 487); it crashes on a method call on a result typed by the intersection of its candidates' return types (row 540); in a family with static parameters, it types such a call by the head of a sort (row 543) and refuses the Meet Rule's case for closed traits (row 546); and its verdict on an overload set can depend on the components compiled before it in the same JVM (row 547). Detail: `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:3185-3240`; `compile-ladder/rung-spec-overloading/decision-record.md` sections 5 to 9.
- F-?1 **The specification gives the run-time instance of a dispatched generic declaration by the POPL 2019 paper's rule.** It builds P-48. Where the value does not fix a type parameter, the rule gives the parameter its bound under the call's static return type. The dispatch paragraph's callout says that both paths take the value's type there instead (row 538, the expected failure `compiler_tests/XXXGenericInstanceUnfixed`). It also says that the compiled path does not yet run its second example, a generic declaration beside a plain one, reached through an argument of static type `Any` (row 496). F-173 gives the inference chapter. Detail: `Specification/basic/overloading.tex:312-349`; `compile-ladder/rung-spec-overloading/decision-record.md` sections 5 to 9.
- F-176 **The specification allows arithmetic in a size, and two size arguments are identical when they are written alike once each operation on numerals is replaced by its value.** It states P-55. By the grammar, a size is a numeral, a name, a sum, a difference, a product, a power to a numeral or a name, or a bracketed size. Two types whose size arguments are so identical are identical. A static parameter is not known to differ from a numeral. F-146 gives the compiled checker, and F-222 walk's arithmetic. When walk infers a size parameter from a call's argument type, it matches a numeral and binds a name, and solves no size written as an operation: read in `IntNat.unifyStaticArg` (`interpreter/evaluator/types/IntNat.java:126-147`), and observed in row 767. - F-223 **The specification's No Duplicates Rule is the papers' non-strict rule, and the compiled checker applies it, to functional methods wherever their `self` parameters stand, abstract ones included, with two exceptions.** By the rule, two declarations of one name may not each be applicable to every call to which the other is, as in the type group's papers of 2011 and 2019 (P-26). The checker refuses such a pair, two functional methods at different `self` positions and an abstract functional method beside a concrete one among them: "There are multiple declarations of f with the same parameter type", naming the domain of the declaration written first. It checks no symbolic operator (row 584), so such a pair of operators passes it and stops the code generator (row 726). It accepts `g[\T\](a: T)` beside `g(a: Any)` and runs the generic one, though it refuses such a pair at a bound below `Any` (row 759). Points that cross entries:

- **The specification's negative integer power.** F-168 says "The integer `^` has no result for a negative power." That was true when rung T revised the number chapters. Since `5ad4a9957`, the integer chapter's method entry gives the result: an exact power at the bases 1 and -1, `DivisionByZero` at 0, and `IntegerOverflow` at any other base (`Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:534-537`, with its callout at `:540-542`). ## F-159, a store for `RR64` alone under a generic factory

- **Scope: fail.** The four probes in report section 3 (`WayANoCast`, `WayACast`, `WayACastSized` and `WayASpec`) declare their own one-method trait `Arr[\T\]` and two stores, `DStore` and `BStore`. They use no trait of the library's arrays (`git show 84aef6a4f^:explorations/reviews/array-design-ways/probes/WayACast.fss`). The compiled runs were in the compiler's own world, with its prelude, because the switch-over has not happened. Each call writes its static argument: `mk[\RR64\](r)`, `mk[\ZZ32\](z)`. The title states none of these conditions. Quoted: "A store written for `RR64` alone is selected under the generic array traits by the library's witness `typecase` and its `cast`, on both paths."
- **Present meaning: fail.** The entry states one measurement in the present tense. The measurement was made on 2026-09-29, on `main` at `6bc21c364` (report section 1). No gated test holds it. The probes and their captures were removed from the tree in `84aef6a4f` and are now only in the history. Quoted: "Wrapped in the library's `cast`, as `additiveIdentity` does, it checks, and both paths pick the `RR64` store only for `RR64`."
- **Evidence: pass.** Report section 3 holds the checker's refusal ("Function body has type OR(DStore,BStore[\T\]), but declared return type is Arr[\T\]") and the output of both paths ("RR64 DStore 1.5", "ZZ32 BStore 7"). The plain-factory sentence agrees with the report: the compiled run dispatches to the plain declaration, walk then refused the pair at load (rows 159 and 475), and "whether it then takes this pair is not measured". The entry does not say what kind of evidence this is: probe programs, observed once. The rewrite should say it.
- **Comprehension: fail.** "Store" is the report's own term (section 0: "the object that holds an array's elements"). The entry and the skill do not define it. "Its union type" has no clear referent: it is the type of the `typecase`'s body, the union of its arms, `OR(DStore,BStore[\T\])`. The entry does not say what a witness is. Quoted: "A witness `typecase` whose `RR64` arm returns that store runs under walk, and the checker refuses its union type."
- **Ownership: pass.** The entry has one subject: how a generic factory selects a store written for one element type (decision A's ways A1 and A2, P-85).

F-229 and row 722 record that such a witness throws `CastError` at its `cast` where walk infers `T` at a value's run-time class. Row 721 says that walk does so for `RR64` values too. For that reason, `array1` and `array2` now take a witness of their result type (F-229). F-159 states neither the static-argument condition nor this limit. I inferred that the probe's device would throw at an inferred `T`; I did not measure it. The rewrite should limit the claim to a written static argument and cite F-229 for the result-type witness, but it should not claim the throw. Quoted: "by the library's witness `typecase` and its `cast`, on both paths". F-27 (walk's load check, not yet run on the pair) and P-85 (decision A open) agree.

== explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md, ## Decisions on record, ### The standard and the sources

POSITIONS.md:24
- P-26 **Where the type group's later positions conflict with the specification's early text, the later positions win.** The early text was a wish. The type group, the part of the team that built the type checker and the compiler, then worked to make the language run, with performance as the goal and specialization a must, and learned what is feasible. Specialization, in the type group's design, is a special version of a generic function for one instantiation, such as `tail(x: List[ZZ])` beside `tail[X](x: List[X])`, which dispatch chooses at run time. Where the two conflict, the specification is revised to follow their later word (P-95 records each change with its reason). Their later word includes the exclusion rule, specialization kept, the number types of the compiler's prelude made siblings in 2009 and 2010 (P-43: the library's numbers are flat in the same way), Karl Naden's 2012 write-up "The Return Type Rule and Generics" (`Papers/Types/journal/justificationOfRTR.tex`) and the type group's POPL 2019 paper (F-166). The implementers' later word also outweighs unfinished text. The revival does not second-guess them: it knows less than they did.

== explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md, ## Decisions on record, ### Numbers

POSITIONS.md:84
- P-80 **The specification's sign-refined number types are a superseded design: a program tests such a subset of a type at run time.** These types are the specification's subtypes by sign, such as positive ℚ, non-negative ℚ and non-zero ℚ, and the same refinements of the integers. The machine types `NN32` and `NN64` are separate types, not among them. The specification's number chapters now test a value's sign by comparison, and a float with two getters of `RR64`: `check` returns `Just(x)` for a finite `x`, `check_star` returns `Just(x)` for an `x` that is not a NaN, and each returns `Nothing` otherwise. The chapter that held the design, `Specification/advanced-lib/numbers-advanced.tex`, stays word for word, marked superseded by a callout in the form of every specification change (P-96), so that the original design stays on record. Built: the chapters' rewrite and the callout (F-168). Their possible return belongs to P-62: once the `covariant` keyword is built, a worker tries to bring them back as covariant static parameters.

POSITIONS.md:82
- P-78 **`SUM` and `PROD` are one generic reduction each over the library's algebra, in place of the team's catch-all over `Number`, and take their identity from the static argument.** `SUM` is generic over `AdditiveGroup` and `PROD` over `MultiplicativeRing`. A reduction written with generators writes its static argument where its generators and body do not fix the element type, as in `SUM[\ZZ32\][j <- 0#n] f(j)`. A declared type that receives the value does not fix it: the compiled checker refuses the call without the static argument even then (gap-ledger row 731). A sum without generators is written as before, with no static argument: `SUM e` over a collection `e`, and the dot product `x DOT y`. `BIG MAXN`, `BIG MINN` and `BIG MINMAXN`, the team's `Number`-typed big operators for the maximum, the minimum and both, each with an identity, are gone; no program called them. `MAX` and `MIN` get no identity on the integers or the floats, so an empty `BIG MAX` or `BIG MIN` raises `EmptyReduction` (F-60: a maximum's identity is its type's least value, which a coercion into a wider type does not carry). Built for the number types. Under walk, an empty `SUM` or `PROD` over another algebra, such as a user `AdditiveGroup`, still fails (gap-ledger row 436) until the specification's `HasIdentity` is built (PLAN, phase 3, the line on `where` clauses).

- F-159 **In probes of 2026-09-29, a generic factory with a written static argument selected a store written for `RR64` alone, through a witness `typecase` wrapped in the library's `cast`, on both paths.** A store is the object that holds an array's elements. The probes declared their own one-method trait `Arr[\T\]` and two stores, `DStore` for `RR64` and a generic `BStore`; they used none of the library's array traits, and the compiled runs used the compiler's own prelude. A witness `typecase` whose `RR64` branch returns `DStore` ran under walk, and the compiled checker refused the type of its body, the union `OR(DStore,BStore[\T\])`. Wrapped in the library's `cast`, as `additiveIdentity` does, it checked, and both paths picked `DStore` only for `mk[\RR64\](r)`. A plain factory beside the generic one also worked compiled; walk's load check (F-27) was not run on that pair. Where walk infers the element type from a value, the library's factories use a witness of their result type instead (F-229). It bears on array decision A (P-85). No gated test holds it, and the probes are in the history before `84aef6a4f`. Detail: `reviews/array-design-ways.md` section 3.
- F-229 **`array1` and `array2` give a vector and a matrix only at the eight number types, chosen by a `typecase` over a witness of their result type; at any other element type they give a plain array.** The branches are `ZZ32`, `ZZ64`, `NN32`, `NN64`, `ZZ`, `QQ`, `RR32` and `RR64`; each builds the array at that type and returns it through `cast`, in `additiveIdentity`'s shape. `Number` and `AnyIntegral` get a plain array, since `Vector[\Number,n\]` is not well-formed under the family's element bound (F-151; row 721). Walk's `Int`, the type that walk infers for an integer value (row 364), gets a plain array too, since no branch is exactly `Int`. The specification's "Array Expressions" makes an array of `Number` elements a vector (row 729, contested). The witness is of the result type, because a witness of the element type would match `Int`, a type below `ZZ32`, and throw `CastError` at the `cast`, as `openRange` does at walk's `Int` (row 722). Gated under walk by `tests/ArrayFactoryNumberTypes` and `ArrayFactoryAbstractNumber`, and for the compiled checker by the distance stage. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-library-factories/REPORT.md` sections 1 (the change), 3 and 4 (the ways measured).
- F-162 **Citing `Specification/library/apis/*.tex` as an independent standard is circular.** The team says that the library part "is largely automatically generated from the API code" (`Specification/library/structure.tex:25-31`). The build renders these listings from the `.fsi` files of `Library/` and `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/`, and the listings are not in the tree. So a listing cannot justify an edit of an `.fsi` file: the edit changes the listing in the next built PDF. Cite the `.fsi` line. The `fortress-repo` skill's `references/specification.md` holds the rule.

In the frozen copy, Appendix I, the changes appendix, is a stub that the team left; in `Specification/` it holds the revival's changes (P-96). `Specification/fortress.pdf` is a draft build, so the team's `\note` boxes print. A third text, the team's unfinished restart, is later on some topics (F-166). The `fortress-repo` skill's `references/specification.md` says how to cite and change each copy. Detail: `reviews/spec-change-form.md` sections 5 and 7.
- F-165 **The repository is a 2018 fork of `sirinath/fortress`, and `main` descends from `8fe1daa8f`, which copied a third-party Java 9 port onto the team's last commit, `a874948ac`.** The port shares no history with this tree, and most of its 1,506 files are removed or redone. One running piece stays, the `FTypeArrayList` fix for the JDK 8 `TreeSet` crash; `lineage.md` lists the rest for removal. The branch `clean-ladder` (`8332bd34f`) rebuilds on `a874948ac` without the port and never replaced `main`. Detail: `coordinator/lineage.md`, "The facts" (the fork, the graft and the port's files), and "Verification against Pavol's recollection (the same worker, re-briefed)", items "Working code" and "Verdict" (the running piece and the removal list).
- F-166 **On the topics of its Types chapter, such as the exclusion rule and covariance, the team's latest word is the unfinished restart, not `Specification/`.** The restart, `Documentation/Specification/`, was never adopted. Its Types chapter restates the exclusion rule as "instantiation exclusion" and adds `covariant`. On static parameters, traits, exceptions, components and the numeric library, `Specification/` is the only statement. The type group's POPL 2019 paper is later than both (F-?1). Detail: `coordinator/spec-lineage.md` section 6.
- F-?1 **The type group's POPL 2019 paper gives P-48's instance rule, and its soundness proof does not cover the library's F-bounded functions, such as `SUM` and `BIG MAX`.** The paper is later than both the specification and the team's restart (F-166). Its calculus does not let a method type parameter occur in an upper bound, so F-bounded method parameters are outside it. It also leaves out top-level functions and functional methods, among other limits. `reviews/decisions-review/popl-recheck.md` checks the curator's decisions against the paper. Detail: `research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019-extract.md` sections 6 and 8.
- F-167 **The specification states instantiation exclusion, and each example that the rule refuses now shows the library's shape beside it; the calculi of Appendix A carry a callout that they predate the rule.** It builds P-97. It also bars a `where`-clause variable from an `extends` clause's static arguments. The refused examples include the covariance example, a subtrait of every instantiation, the empty list, the empty optional value and the root's algebra. Each stays, marked "Not allowed", beside the library's shape, which runs on both paths except `Nothing[\String\]` on the compiled prelude (row 331). The checker does not yet refuse two cases: an object that extends two instantiations that differ only in a `bool` argument (row 406), and one that extends two instantiations of one trait, one of whose arguments is a static parameter (row 414). Detail and examples: `compile-ladder/rung-spec-route-a/decision-record.md` sections 2 and 3; its section 4.2 (the calculi's callout).
- F-168 **The specification's number chapters describe the flat library, and its advanced chapter on rational quantities stays word for word as a superseded design.** The eight number types are siblings under `Number` (F-131). They convert by the library's coercions (P-74), and every other conversion is explicit, such as `asFloat(x)`. The sign-refined types, such as positive ℚ, are gone; a program tests a value's sign at run time (P-80). ℚ holds +∞, −∞ and 0/0, and claims neither a field nor a total order. `QQ` extends the four algebraic traits that the library declares on it, and their laws hold for the finite rationals. F-172 gives the integer chapter's rules. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-spec-numbers/decision-record.md` section 3; `Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:224-229` (ℚ's traits).
- F-169 **The Working Draft never wrote static-argument inference, never named the type that a library gives an integer numeral, and never named a range's integer type; the specification's text on these is the revival's.** The Working Draft's inference chapter is a heading and notes. It described numeral types, such as `NaturalNumeral[\n,10,v\]`, but did not relate them to the number types, and its ranges section names no integer type. The later restart adds nothing on the three. So a citation of the specification on them cites the revival, not the team. The revised text states F-173's inference rule and F-170's ranges, and gives an integer numeral the type `IntLiteral` (P-76). Detail: `reviews/numerics-plan-coordinator/evidence-B.md` sections 1 and 2; `Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:154-156` (the callout on the numeral types).
- F-170 **The specification's ranges are over ℤ32, and its own ranges over wider integer types are respelled.** An integer numeral and a `nat` or `int` parameter convert into a range's ℤ32 components (row 485, fixed). Another integer type is a static error. A loop whose counter must have a wider integer type runs over a range of ℤ32 values and widens each element. The two examples that built `ZZ64` ranges run over ℤ32, and `ant testSpecData`, a gate step, runs both (F-114). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-spec-ranges/decision-record.md` sections 2 and 3; `Specification/basic/expressions/ranges.tex:42-58` and `:88-109`.
- F-171 **The specification reads a `comprises` clause as the restart's Types chapter does: every value of the trait is a value of a listed type.** So a trait with static parameters may extend the closed trait without being listed, if at least one type extends it and every type that extends it is below a listed type. A listed type may be an instantiation at the trait's static parameters or `where`-clause variables. The text does not say whether a bare type variable may be listed; walk overflows its stack on one (row 407). The compiled checker departs in three ways: it checks only the closed trait's immediate subtypes (row 487), it reads the clause in the subtrait's own type-variable names (row 489), and it finds extenders by the simple text of a name (row 490). Whether the team's commented `comprises Integral[\I\] where [\I\]` is valid is open (F-121). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-spec-comprises/decision-record.md` section 2.
- F-172 **The specification's integer chapter states the library's integer rules.** It states `narrow`, `LSHIFT` and `RSHIFT` on the five integer types, `shift` exact at any count, and nonnegative `GCD` and `LCM`. A fixed-size result that the type cannot hold throws `IntegerOverflow`. At a negative power, the bases 1 and -1 give their exact power, a base of 0 throws `DivisionByZero`, and any other base throws `IntegerOverflow`; F-263 gives the library's power under walk. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-spec-integer-rules/decision-record.md` section 2; `Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:530-542` (the power).
- F-?2 **The coercion example of the specification's "Coercion Resolution", over `ZZ32`, `ZZ64` and `ZZ128`, declares the exclusions that the chapter's definitions need: `ZZ32 excludes { ZZ64, ZZ128 }` and `ZZ64 excludes { ZZ128 }`.** The chapter defines rejection, and so which declaration is no less specific, through exclusion. In a probe of the rung, the revised example ran as printed on both paths, `f(S32Of) = 1`. Under walk, `tests/CoercionMostSpecificRungC.fss` gates it (row 394, fixed). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-spec-integer-rules/decision-record.md` section 2, decision 6; `Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:500-516` and `:580` onward.
